applicant_utility.summary: A full-cost four-year doctoral package at University of Galway: a €25,000 annual stipend plus tuition, for a 1 September start. The application is only complete once your supervisor form and two academic reference forms have reached hrscholar@universityofgalway.ie, so the effective deadline for you is weeks earlier than the published closing date because you cannot submit those forms yourself. Treat the scholarship and the Structured PhD admission as two separate wins you both need.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year or recently graduated students holding a first or upper second class honours degree who have already identified a University of Galway supervisor willing to take them on for a 1 September start.
application_readiness_checklist: Read the Applicant's Guide 2026 in full before touching the form; the University requires it and assesses adherence to its word and page limits
Contact a potential supervisor directly through universityofgalway.ie/findasupervisor and confirm they will submit the supervisor form before the deadline
Ask two referees early and confirm they will email their forms directly; the office will not tell you whether forms have arrived
Draft the personal research statement to a hard 1,000-word limit, and push endnotes, bibliography and appendices into the 'any other relevant information' section instead
Book the separate Structured PhD admission application well before 1 September if you need a visa, since the PhD decision and the visa decision each take weeks
common_rejection_risks: Application ruled incomplete because the supervisor form or one of the two reference forms was missing or late; HR Scholar will not check or confirm receipt for you
Being a currently registered PhD student, or having previously held a PhD, which is an outright bar
Proposing a supervisor who also acts as a referee, which the University explicitly rules out
Applying for the scholarship but not the Structured PhD programme, or vice versa, and losing the award on entry requirements
Part-time PhD intent, which makes the scholarship unavailable
Exceeding the 1,000-word research statement limit, which can mean part of the application is not assessed
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The student levy and any consumables or travel budget are explicitly not funded, and a separate application fee applies for admission to the Structured PhD programme (the scholarship itself carries no application fee).
document_audit: The supervisor form must come from the proposed supervisor - anything you send on their behalf is disregarded
The two reference forms must come from the referees themselves; a referee can be an employer or other non-academic if they can speak to your academic suitability
The first application you submit is final: no corrections, no re-submission
Supervisors must be eligible primary supervisors under QA245 and confirm that on the supervisor form, so check this before nominating
alerts: A proposed supervisor can have several applicants in a year but normally only one awardee, so ask whether they already have a strong candidate
No extensions are possible for you, the supervisor or the referees - one shared deadline
No feedback is provided on the application or the interview, so work with your supervisor rather than requesting a debrief
Interviews sit in a narrow mid-to-late April window; if you need notice for work or visa reasons, expect very little
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the application, supervisor form and two reference forms to hrscholar@universityofgalway.ie by 17:00 Irish time on the closing date; completeness is confirmed by email in late February, interviews run 16-27 April and outcomes are issued in late May.

Eligible direct research expenses of €5,000 per annum
eligibility: Suitably qualified applicants pursuing a postdoctoral fellowship at an eligible research body in Ireland for either one or two years
Funding across all disciplines, from archaeology to zoology
Pioneering proposals addressing new and emerging fields of research, or introducing creative and innovative approaches, are welcomed
Proposals of an interdisciplinary nature are encouraged

Mentor form completed before the mentor deadline
Research office endorsement completed before the research office deadline
Indicative application form matching the fellowship duration requested (separate one-year and two-year forms are published)
documents: Completed online application form submitted through the Research Ireland online system
Indicative mentor form completed by the proposed mentor
Research office endorsement from the host research body
selection_criteria: An objective selection process using international, independent expert peer review
Excellence of the research proposed by the applicant
coverage: Salary of €47,273 in year one and €47,880 in year two, corresponding to points 1 and 2 on the Postdoctoral Researcher Level 2A of the Research Ireland team members salary scale
Eligible direct research expenses of €5,000 per annum
application_method: Submit the application through the Research Ireland online system by the applicant deadline

official.research_requirement: An applicant-led research proposal in any discipline; pioneering, innovative and interdisciplinary proposals are welcomed
official.description: The Government of Ireland Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme is an established national initiative, funded by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science and managed by Research Ireland, supporting suitably qualified applicants to pursue a postdoctoral fellowship at an eligible research body in Ireland for either one or two years.

applicant_utility.summary: A one- or two-year named postdoctoral fellowship at an eligible Irish research body, paid as a salary of €47,273 in year one and €47,880 in year two, plus employer PRSI and €5,000 a year of eligible direct research expenses. The award is made to you personally rather than to a project, so the proposal has to survive international, independent expert peer review on its own merits. The route runs through your proposed mentor and the host research office, whose endorsements fall due after yours, so plan backwards from their deadlines rather than yours.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers with a completed doctorate and a genuinely bottom-up idea in any discipline who can secure a mentor and a research office endorsement at an eligible Irish research body.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm with your host institution that it is an eligible research body before you invest in writing
Agree the mentor's participation and get the indicative mentor form drafted well before the 6 November mentor deadline
Brief the research office early, since its endorsement closes on 13 November, after your own submission
Use the indicative application form that matches the duration you want - the one-year and two-year forms are separate documents
Budget how you will use the €5,000 annual research expenses, since eligible direct costs are unlikely to stretch to everything
common_rejection_risks: Framing the proposal as directed or project-tied work when the programme explicitly funds bottom-up, non-directed research
A mentor form or research office endorsement that misses its own deadline, which invalidates an otherwise strong applicant submission
Requesting two years when the proposal only supports one, which weakens peer review
Choosing a host body that is not on the eligible research body list
Writing for a national panel rather than international independent reviewers who may not know your sub-field
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the salary, employer PRSI and the €5,000 annual research expenses, including relocation, accommodation and conference travel.
document_audit: The indicative mentor form and research office endorsement are separate submissions on separate deadlines, both after yours
The correct indicative form for the requested duration must be used
Read the Applicants guide to the online system and the ROs guide, since the portal splits responsibilities between applicant, mentor and research office
alerts: The salary corresponds to points 1 and 2 of the Research Ireland Postdoctoral Researcher Level 2A scale and may change under the current national pay agreement, so year-two figures can move
The call is annual but no next-call date is published, so watch the Research Ireland funding and news pages from late summer
FAQ questions had their own 16 October deadline, so use the published FAQ rather than emailing after that date
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit through the Research Ireland online system by the applicant deadline, then the mentor form by the mentor deadline and the research office endorsement by the research office deadline; outcomes are issued at the end of April for a 1 September start.
